comment: Health systems chronically overspend on initial builds and underspend on ongoing operations. Without dedicated, recurring operational funding to manage software version alignment, continuous semantic normalization, local code mapping, and compliance auditing, shared national infrastructure inevitably degrades back into fragmented, non-comparable silos once short-term capital grants run out.

public.text: Health systems chronically overspend on initial builds and underspend on ongoing operations. Without dedicated, recurring operational funding to manage software version alignment, continuous semantic normalization, local code mapping, and compliance auditing, shared national infrastructure inevitably degrades back into fragmented, non-comparable silos once short-term capital grants run out.
public.suggestedRevision: Add to guidance on financing: “Guidance on financing must explicitly distinguish between Initiation (Capital Build) and Maintenance (Ongoing Run-Rate) phases. Guidelines should advise member states that any capital investment in DPI-H components should be tethered to a secured, recurring operational maintenance budget to prevent system divergence and technological decay.”
